theme: Tesla's capex cut and record energy margin meet Meta's first cash burn in years, while bitcoin sits right on the ETF and treasury-company cost basis near $80K.

items.title: Bitcoin cost basis by holder
items.picked: Glassnode data trending on X today says bitcoin is testing the spot ETF cost basis near $81K, and that treasury companies are back above their roughly $80K cost basis but aren't buying. This chart tracks those same average-cost lines.
items.matters: When the price sits right on the average cost of the biggest holder groups, it decides whether they are in profit or underwater. That shapes ETF flows and how easily treasury companies can raise money to buy more.
items.know: As of Oct 14 the sheet has iShares IBIT's average cost at $81,126, treasury companies at $80,382, all public companies at $78,881, all US spot ETFs at $76,645 and Strategy at $75,444, with BTC at $81,562. Glassnode's ~$81K ETF figure lines up with the IBIT line, not the sheet's lower all-ETF line, so methods differ. The weekly data is about a week old; BTC traded near $82K this morning after touching $84.8K on Oct 21.

items.title: Strategy's weekly bitcoin buys vs sales
items.picked: Treasury companies are back in profit but barely buying, and Strategy is the clearest example. Its Oct 19 filing showed only 267 BTC bought for $22.1M, while it spent $193.1M buying back STRC preferred stock and raised its buyback authorization to $3B.
items.matters: Strategy's weekly buying has been one of bitcoin's steadiest sources of demand. Small buys alongside much larger preferred buybacks show where its cash is going right now.
items.know: The ledger runs through the Oct 12 filing (250 BTC at $86,194) and doesn't include the Oct 19 purchase yet. The chart counts 6,948 BTC sold since Jan 2025, nearly all in four weekly sales between Jun 30 and Aug 10, 2026, before buying resumed with 4,603 BTC on Aug 31. Holdings were 848,250 BTC after Oct 12; the Oct 19 filing put them at 848,517.

items.title: Bitcoin vs its 200-week moving average
items.picked: Michael Saylor said this week that the next bull market has started, pointing to bitcoin's roughly $20,000 rebound from its 200-week moving average. This chart shows that line.
items.matters: The 200-week average has marked the bottom zone in past cycles, so how far the price sits above it is a common gauge of cycle risk and of how much room there is to fall.
items.know: In the latest weekly row (week of Oct 16), BTC was $81,475 against a 200-week average of $66,710, a ratio of 1.22x, up from 1.19x in mid-September. The chart uses a log scale, and the data ends before this week's move to $84.8K and back to about $82K.

items.title: Tesla free cash flow, trailing four quarters
items.picked: Tesla reported Q3 last night with free cash flow of $1.53B, far above the roughly -$4.9B analysts expected, because capex came in at $4.7B instead of about $8B. It also cut 2026 capex guidance to about $20B from more than $25B, and the stock was down about 5% premarket.
items.matters: Free cash flow is what funds robotaxi, Optimus, AI compute and Terafab without raising money, and it matters more if a merger with capital-hungry SpaceX goes ahead. Musk said spending will become more meaningful next year and reach the tens of billions in 2028.
items.know: The chart already includes Q3: trailing-four-quarter free cash flow was $3.30B at Sep 30, 2026, down from $7.0B in March, as trailing capex rose to $15.4B while operating cash flow held near $18.7B. The peak was $8.9B in Sep 2022.

items.title: Tesla gross margin: automotive vs energy
items.picked: Energy was a standout in Tesla's Q3: 13.7 GWh deployed, its highest-ever order rate and backlog, and the CFO described extreme demand from data centers. Energy gross margin jumped to 33.1% from 20.4% in Q2.
items.matters: Energy storage earns much higher margins than cars and is tied directly to the AI data center buildout. That gives Tesla an AI-linked business that is already profitable today.
items.know: The chart includes Q3: energy gross margin was 33.1% versus 18.0% for automotive. Tesla said part of the jump came from tariff refunds and warranty true-downs, so not all of it repeats. The energy margin swings a lot from quarter to quarter (39.5% in Q1 2026, 20.4% in Q2).

items.title: Cybercabs on the Texas robotaxi registry
items.picked: On last night's call Musk said the Cybercab fleet in Austin has grown by a factor of 10, and Tesla said cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles grew eightfold in Q3 to nearly 2 million.
items.matters: State registrations are the earliest public sign of how fast Tesla is putting Cybercabs on the road, ahead of its own fleet numbers.
items.know: The Texas DMV registry count went from 45 on Aug 31 to 319 on Oct 8, 2026. The data is two weeks old, and registered vehicles are not the same as vehicles actively giving rides.

items.title: SpaceX since its IPO vs Tesla and the Nasdaq-100
items.picked: The two Musk stocks split after earnings. SpaceX was up 9.8% on Oct 21 after its first profitable quarter as a public company and Musk's merger comments, while Tesla was down about 5% premarket today after its capex cut.
items.matters: If the boards' special committees pursue a merger, the exchange ratio would depend on how the two stocks trade against each other, so the gap between them is now closely watched.
items.know: Through Oct 20 the sheet has SPCX at 109.5 (9.5% above its $135 IPO price), Tesla at 93.6 and the Nasdaq-100 at 100.2, all indexed to Jun 11, 2026. SPCX peaked at 156.6 on Jun 16. The image ends in mid-October, and neither it nor the data includes the post-earnings moves.

items.title: Meta: operating cash flow, capex and free cash flow
items.picked: Meta reported Q3 last night: revenue rose 26% to $64.6B, but capex of $34.9B topped operating cash flow of $32.8B, so free cash flow was negative $2.1B. That would be the first negative quarter on this chart, which goes back to 2019.
items.matters: Meta is now the clearest case of AI spending using up all of a megacap's cash flow, which is the core worry behind the AI trade.
items.know: The sheet stops at Q2 2026 (Jun 30), when free cash flow was $1.75B on $31.9B of operating cash flow and $30.1B of capex; Q3 isn't in yet. The sheet computes FCF as operating cash flow minus capex, which can differ slightly from Meta's own figure because Meta also subtracts finance-lease principal payments.

items.title: Neocloud debt vs cash
items.picked: Nvidia's Jensen Huang told CNBC today that demand for neoclouds is 'off the charts' but capital is scarce. CoreWeave was at the center of last week's AI-stock selloff over concerns about its finances.
items.matters: Neoclouds borrow heavily to buy GPUs, so higher borrowing costs and pickier lenders hit them first. This chart shows which ones have the thinnest cushion.
items.know: CoreWeave carries $35.6B of debt against $5.5B of cash and Cipher $5.4B against $0.8B, while Nebius is nearly matched at $8.5B against $8.0B. Most balance sheets are as of Jun 30, 2026 (Applied Digital Aug 31, TeraWulf Mar 31), and CoreWeave's large lease liabilities aren't included.

items.title: Chip stocks vs the S&P 500
items.picked: Chip stocks bounced on Oct 21 after Super Micro raised its revenue forecast, but Reuters noted the Philadelphia semiconductor index had just fallen eight sessions in a row, its longest losing streak in 18 years.
items.matters: Semis have led the AI bull market, so their strength against the S&P 500 is a quick read on whether the AI trade is cracking or just resetting.
items.know: On monthly data, the SOXX-to-SPY ratio hit a record 327.8 in June 2026 and was 246.5 in the October row, with SOXX 23% below its high. October is a partial month, and the image was exported Oct 19.
